description: A droplet of lung surfactant is deposited on a sharp-edged pedestal, forming a surfactant film at its air-water surface. The film is cycled continuously to mimic breathing. Surface tension values (minimum and maximum) are obtained by real-time drop shape analysis.

title: Surfactant Adsorption Test
description: A fluorescence-based high-throughput method measuring the extent and rate of adsorption of lung surfactant at the air-liquid interface. Lung surfactant labelled with a fluorescent probe is injected into multi-well plates containing a light-absorbing agent (brilliant black). Fluorescence of surfactant reaching the surface is measured; bulk fluorescence is quenched by the light-absorbing agent.

title: Atomic Force Microscopy (AFM) of Surfactant Films
description: The topography of surfactant structures formed at respiratory-like air-liquid interfaces upon exposure to test substances is studied by atomic force microscopy on fixed samples, providing nanoscale structural information about the surfactant film.

title: Langmuir-Blodgett Film / Langmuir Trough
description: Interfacial films of surfactant are transferred from the air-liquid interface onto solid supports or studied in a Langmuir trough. Surfactant films are compressed by reducing surface area, and a sensor plate measures surface pressure variations to yield surface pressure-area isotherms. Comparison in the presence or absence of test substances reveals interactions with lung surfactant at the molecular level. Can be combined with epifluorescence or atomic force microscopy.

title: Cryogenic Transmission Electron Microscopy (Cryo-TEM)
description: Lung surfactant vesicles in aqueous dispersions are incubated with test substance, applied onto a carbon grid, and vitrified in liquid ethane cooled by liquid nitrogen. Morphological and structural changes at the single membrane vesicle level (size, circularity, lamellarity) are visualized to indicate disruption of three-dimensional surfactant structures.

title: Differential Scanning Calorimetry (DSC)
description: Phase transitions occurring in lipid membranes (such as lung surfactant models) are studied over changes in temperature. Thermotropic phase behaviours of phospholipids in surfactant models are characterized in the absence or presence of interacting substances. Associated enthalpy, transition temperature, and cooperativity are estimated from thermograms.

title: Histological detection of atelectasis in lung tissue
description: Lung tissue from exposed experimental animals is stained and examined histologically to identify areas of alveolar collapse (atelectasis). Individual alveoli cannot be measured directly due to their small size (~200 µm diameter), but regions of atelectasis are observable at the tissue level.
